## Overview

Weeks 2 and 3 focus on plate streaking, colony observation, and starting liquid cultures for later growth analysis.

## Purpose

- Recover and propagate *Delftia acidovorans* from colonies.
- Observe colony morphology, streak plates, and start liquid cultures.
- Review safety procedures for working with live microbial isolates.

## Learning Outcomes

- **List** the items needed to propagate microbes in liquid cultures and 96-well plates.
- **Explain** the stages of bacterial growth on a growth-curve graph.
- **Describe** defined, complex, selective, enriched, and differential media.
- **Discuss** the importance of controls.
- **Practice** inoculating and diluting liquid cultures.
- **Describe** the purpose, methods, and preliminary results of microbial growth experiments.
- **Collect** and **interpret** colony morphology and growth data.
- **Create** and **use** a team data management plan.

## Skills and Knowledge

### Skills

- Work safely with bacterial growth on agar plates.
- Document protocols and results clearly.
- Interpret colony morphology and growth in liquid TSB medium.
- Propagate bacteria in liquid culture.

### Knowledge

- PPE for microbial work.
- Loop use, sterilization, and streaking methods.
- Propagation of microorganisms in solid and liquid media.

## Task

Review the protocol before lab and work with your partner to complete the propagation tasks, document observations, and record changes to the procedure.

## Criteria for Success

You should complete the solid- and liquid-media propagation tasks, collect observations that can be analyzed, and submit a complete ELN entry.

## Background

Our lab experiments will use the bacterium *Delftia acidovorans*. Since we will work with environmental isolates that may be naturally antibiotic-resistant, we want to minimize exposure and contain any potential biohazards. We will work with several different isolates. Each group will characterize one isolate.

## Procedures

### Lab Safety

#### Before Lab

:::{.callout-caution}
Note that we will be working with live microbial isolates today. Please follow all safety protocols and dispose of potentially biohazardous materials properly.
:::
- Wear a lab coat, goggles, and gloves.
- Wipe the bench and pipettors with 70% ethanol.

#### During Lab

- Treat all tips as potential biohazards.
- Remove PPE when leaving the lab.
- Discard samples and disposables in the correct containers.
- Keep personal item use to a minimum.

#### After Lab

- Wipe the station with 70% ethanol.
- Decontaminate any personal items touched during lab.
- Dispose of gloves in the main biohazard container.

### Methods: Observe Colony Morphology

1. Place the plate on a bench that has been wiped with 70% ethanol
2. Obtain a TSA plate with colonies of your isolate
3. Observe colonies without opening the plate and record notes
4. Photograph the plate using a black background if provided
5. Share images with your partner and compare observations

### Methods: Plate Streaking

Figure @fig-module2-streaking illustrates the transfer of a single colony to a fresh plate during the streaking workflow.

![Single-colony transfer onto a fresh TSA plate for streaking practice. Created with BioRender.com.](images/PlateStreaking.png){#fig-module2-streaking fig-alt="Diagram showing a sterile loop transferring a single colony onto a fresh agar plate for streaking practice."}

1. Obtain a sterile loop. Do not touch the loop to any other surface
2. Open the plate slightly and pick a single colony
3. Streak onto a fresh TSA plate
4. Close and label the plate with name, class, and date

Remember to label your plates with enough information for someone to understand what is growing and since when!

### Methods: Plate Labeling

Figure @fig-module2-labeling shows the correct placement and content of labels on the bottom of an agar plate.

![Correct placement of labels on the bottom of a TSA plate. Created with BioRender.com.](images/PlateLabeling.png){#fig-module2-labeling fig-alt="Diagram showing how to label the bottom of an agar plate with isolate name, section, group number, and date."}

1. Write on the **bottom** of the plate with a permanent marker.
2. Include your **isolate name, class section, group number, and the date.**
3. Keep labels near the edge so they do not obscure the agar surface.
4. Photograph the labeled bottom for your ELN record.

### Methods: Starting a Liquid Culture

1. Obtain Tryptic Soy Broth (TSB) and sterile culture tubes
2. Label three tubes
3. TSB Control (date, initials)
4. Your isolate (date, initials). For example: _Delftia acidovorans_ SPH-1 (date, initials)
5. Use a sterile loop to inoculate the media. Work quickly to avoid contamination
6. Cap to the first stop
7. Place tubes in the shaking incubator at 30 degrees Celsius for 24 hours
8. Next session, compare shaking versus static growth
9. Write your procedure notes below

## Data
Record observations of colony morphology:

- Color
- Size range
- Shape
- Edges
- Texture or sheen
- Other observations

Liquid culture setup
- Tube labels used
- Inoculation notes
- Shaking versus static plan
- Start time
